claim_short: Fourier conduction is parabolic with formally infinite propagation speed
note: standard; a diffusion equation has no characteristic speed at all, so 'infinite' is a statement about the absence of a speed, not a measured one

claim_short: the thermal field satisfies a parabolic equation predicting infinite thermal propagation speed
note: same

claim_short: the LS/Cattaneo law gives a finite thermal characteristic speed when tau0>0
compared_with: V-B2a (c_h=sqrt(kappa/tau0)=354.14 m/s for the steel set)
note: finite, and the value is the one (4.6) gives; the statement is scoped 'for the displayed law', which is the right scope

claim_short: tau0>0 gives a finite characteristic speed for the thermal branch, but is not by itself a proof of well-posedness
note: correct distinction, and rarely drawn. Note the contrast with DPL, where the analogous one-line conclusion is FALSE (V-B2p: first-order-in-both DPL is unconditionally stable but has infinite propagation speed)

claim_short: the second relaxation time enters the stress through the temperature rate and does not introduce a second temperature field
note: correct, and it is the right way to block the two-temperature conflation

compared_with: V-B3d (D==0 to 1e-16 for the standard quadratic energy)
note: right hedge: for the standard GN-II free energy the dissipation is identically zero, which I verified numerically. It is not zero for arbitrary added terms, so 'described as' is honest

claim_short: wave attenuation and energy conservation for GN-II must be obtained from the specific model and BVP
the relation of GN-III to types I/II and its dissipation properties 'depend on the precise formulation'
note: with k*>0 GN-III is dissipative and with k*->0 it reduces to GN-II: that limit IS universal in the family and one sentence would remove the vagueness. As written it is not false, only vague

claim_short: no single dissipation expression or parameter-ordering condition applies to generalized thermoelasticity
note: CONFIRMED-WRONG and now the strongest content defect in the file. Counterexamples inside the reviewed family: GL's tau1 >= tau0 (S1, S2, both open-access and explicit); DPL's tau_theta > tau_q/2 (Quintanilla & Racke; my V-B2p re-derivation); LS's tau0>0 with non-negative entropy production. claim_short: the dissipation inequality restricts admissible constitutive relations and must hold for all processes
Coleman-Noll restrictions from requiring the inequality for arbitrary strain rate and temperature rate
note: valid for psi=psi(eps,T). It cannot deliver GL/GN/DPL, whose free energies depend on Tdot or on alpha. The section presents it as the general route; it is the classical special case

claim_short: the P speed exceeds the S speed since lambda+2mu>mu for stable materials
note: follows from lambda+2mu/3>0 and mu>0, as stated

claim_short: C^u is a positive-definite interfacial stiffness (Pa/m)
note: positive-definiteness is assumed, not derived; for an interface layer with negative stiffness (a buckling film) it fails, and then the reflection problem has an exponentially growing solution

claim_short: formal limits (tau0->0, fractional order, etc.) are only meaningful after each constitutive law and admissible range is stated
positivity or monotonicity of a kernel is not a general sufficient proof of a well-posed IBVP
a finite-horizon derivative does not by itself imply finite propagation speed
note: true and important: the MDD kernel is a moving average, which is a smoothing (low-pass) operator, not a transport operator

claim_short: the nonlocal phase speed tends to zero as k->inf while omega tends to c0/xi
note: verified: omega=c0 k/sqrt(1+xi^2k^2) -> c0/xi, c=omega/k -> 0. The correct and unusual statement - nonlocality low-passes the spectrum instead of making it finite-speed, and the text says so

claim_short: for a well-posed interface problem the number of independent conditions must equal the number of unknown amplitudes
note: true but content-free as written: the count has to be done PER DECOUPLED FAMILY (SH: 2 modes, 2 conditions; P-SV-T: 6 modes, 6 conditions), and it fails for MGT-type interfaces where the displacement-gradient data add conditions without adding branches. V-B3e does the census; the text does not

note: correct, and it is exactly how the defects in EQ-077 were found - the identity is a better detector than any single equation check
